source_unit_handling: ASSUMPTION: no vertical CRS in header; z assumed to use the horizontal unit (metre). Override with --z-unit.
vertical.transformation: none: LAS elevations are only unit-scaled to metres
vertical.warning: Elevations are in the source vertical reference (UNKNOWN; not declared in the LAS header). They are not WGS84 ellipsoidal heights; convert (e.g. add a geoid separation) before placing on an ellipsoid-height globe.

origin.note: Model (0,0,0) is this point. Rounded to 100 m / 1 m for readability; exact values.

model_axes.units: metre (grid metres of the working CRS)

glb.mesh: one shared unit box: x,z in [-0.5,0.5], y in [0,1] (base-anchored)
glb.instancing: EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing (required). buildings_compat.glb (optional) uses one node per building instead.
glb.translation: model position of the footprint centre at base elevation
glb.rotation: unit quaternion (0, sin(a/2), 0, cos(a/2)) with a = rotation_deg in radians: yaw about +Y only
glb.scale: (length_m, height_m, width_m): local +X = length axis, +Y = height, +Z = width axis
glb.float_precision: float32 model coordinates relative to the origin (~1e-4 m within a few km)

rotation_convention: rotation_deg: degrees, counter-clockwise viewed from above, from the +grid-easting axis to the box length axis, range [0,180) (a rectangle repeats every 180 deg). Relative to GRID north of the working CRS, not true north. true_bearing_deg in buildings.csv.gz is the length-axis bearing clockwise from TRUE north, [0,180).
grid_convergence_definition: bearing of true north measured clockwise from grid north; true_bearing = grid_bearing - convergence
scale_note: Model distances are projection grid distances; ellipsoidal ground distance ~= grid distance / scale factor.
lonlat_procedure: pyproj.Transformer.from_crs(working_crs, 'EPSG:4326', always_xy=True).transform(easting, northing) -> (longitude, latitude) in degrees. Horizontal only.
placement_instructions: A GLB does not position itself on a map: use the origin and conventions in this file.
Option A (projected-CRS renderers / GIS): place model point (x,y,z) at easting=E0+x, northing=N0-z, elevation=H0+y in the working CRS.

Option B (globe / ENU renderers): build an East-North-Up frame at origin.wgs84_longitude_latitude with height = origin elevation converted to the renderer's height reference; map glTF +X->East, +Y->Up, -Z->North; then yaw the model by +grid_convergence_at_origin_deg (counter-clockwise from above) so grid north lines up with true north, and optionally scale horizontally by 1/point_scale_factor_at_origin. Residual distortion grows with distance from the origin.
Option C: place buildings individually from footprints.geojson (WGS84 lon/lat) or buildings.csv.gz.
Verify alignment against independent map data before relying on it; this tool has not verified it.
instance_mapping: GLB instance i (accessor element i) <-> buildings.csv.gz row with instance_index == i; building_id is derived from the rounded centre and is stable across reruns with identical results.
